title: Rasam

ingredients.title: For the Rasam
items: Tamarind pulp – 2 tbsp, soaked in 1 cup warm water and strained
Toor dal (split pigeon peas) – ¼ cup, cooked and mashed

ingredients.title: For Tempering
items: Fresh coriander leaves – a handful, chopped

instruction.title: Cook the Toor Dal
steps: Rinse the toor dal thoroughly.
Pressure cook with enough water until completely soft, about 3–4 whistles.
Mash the cooked dal until smooth and set aside.

instruction.title: Prepare the Tamarind Water
steps: Soak tamarind in 1 cup warm water for about 10 minutes.
Squeeze the soaked tamarind thoroughly to extract the pulp.
Strain the liquid and discard the fibrous solids.

instruction.title: Prepare the Rasam Base
steps: Add tamarind water, chopped tomato, turmeric powder, and salt to a pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 5–7 minutes until the tomatoes soften and the raw tamarind aroma mellows.

instruction.title: Add Dal & Spices
steps: Add the mashed toor dal and rasam powder.
Add the remaining water and adjust the quantity according to the desired consistency.
Stir well and simmer gently for about 5 minutes.
Avoid prolonged boiling after adding the dal so the rasam retains its light, aromatic character.

instruction.title: Prepare the Tempering
steps: Heat ghee or oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add cumin seeds, broken dry red chilies, crushed garlic, curry leaves, and asafoetida.
Sauté until aromatic and the garlic turns lightly golden.

instruction.title: Finish the Rasam
steps: Pour the hot tempering over the simmering rasam.
Add jaggery or sugar if using to balance the tang.
Adjust salt to taste.
Turn off the heat.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.

instruction.title: Serve
steps: Serve the rasam hot with steamed rice.
Alternatively, serve it on its own as a spicy, tangy South Indian-style soup.

instruction.title: Make Homemade Rasam Powder
steps: Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, dry red chilies, and toor dal separately until fragrant.
Allow the roasted spices to cool completely.
Grind them together into a fine or slightly coarse powder.
Store the rasam powder in an airtight container and use as needed.

chefTips: Tamarind: Strain the tamarind water well for a smooth rasam without fibrous pieces.
Balance: A small amount of jaggery or sugar can soften excessive sourness without making the rasam sweet.
Tempering: Freshly tempered mustard, cumin, curry leaves, and garlic provide much of the rasam's characteristic aroma.
Dal: Use well-cooked and mashed toor dal for a smooth, lightly creamy body.
Boiling: Avoid vigorously boiling the rasam for too long after adding the dal and spices; gentle simmering preserves the aroma.
Serving: Rasam is best served piping hot with steamed rice or enjoyed as a light, spicy soup.
